passages.heading: Static Data Members
passages.why: The default non-orthogonality threshold of the mesh check is 70 degrees, the limit the studio's mesh gate uses.

passages.heading: Private Member Functions
passages.why: In the code under this comment a face beyond 70 degrees is counted as severely non-orthogonal and reported, but the check fails only for faces at 90 degrees or more; the studio's gate is stricter and refuses the mesh at 70.

passages.heading: Static Data Members
passages.why: The default skewness threshold of the mesh check is 4, the second hard limit of the studio's mesh gate.

passages.heading: Static Data Members
passages.why: The default aspect-ratio threshold is 1000; thin cells next to the wall can exceed it, and the studio's gate does not fail on it.

passages.heading: Private Member Functions
passages.text: // This does not cause trouble but is a good indication of a poor mesh.
passages.why: The source describes high skewness as a sign of a poor mesh, not as something that stops a run; the check still reports failure above 4, as the studio's gate does.
